title: Peer Reviewers - Emerging Infectious Diseases journal - CDC
content: Emerging Infectious Disease journal ISSN: 1080-6059 Peer Reviewers Reviewing a Manuscript Peer reviewers for Emerging Infectious Diseases (EID) evaluate manuscripts on EID Manuscript Central , which is a manuscript tracking system that allows authors to submit manuscripts and reviewers to evaluate manuscripts electronically. EID manuscripts must be submitted and reviewed through this system. Reviewers log in, read their assigned manuscript, and recommend to the editors whether EID should accept, reject, or revise the manuscript (reviewers should direct such recommendations for decision only to the editors, not to the authors). Assessments should include comments to the authors on the originality and relevance of the manuscript, clarity of the presentation, logic, and conclusions, and adequacy of methods in the body of the paper, figures, tables, and all supplemental appendices and materials. The journal's editors may edit reviews for tone, length, and language. EID copy editors will ensure that accepted papers are grammatically correct and follow EID style conventions, so reviewers need not to address those areas in detail. Reviewers must maintain an account in EID Manuscript Central . Before beginning a review, reviewers should check to ensure that their information, including email address and affiliations, are correct. Reviewers who have difficulty accessing their account should not create a new one but should instead contact EID’s editorial office for assistance by email at eideditor@cdc.gov. EID Peer Review Standards and Ethics In general, EID follows the current recommendations of the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) . All EID reviewers must read and follow these recommendations. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Peer Review ICMJE recommendations on the use of AI in peer review , as noted below: Because manuscripts submitted to journals are authors' privileged communication, using AI tools in the processing or evaluations of manuscripts may violate confidentiality. Editors, reviewers, or publishers should not upload submitted manuscript into AI systems where confidentiality cannot be assured without authors' explicit permission. [R]eviewers should be transparent in their use of AI tools at any stage of the editorial process, including manuscript preparation, editing, and review. When AI is used, users should disclose which tool was used, and for what purpose. EID reviewers need not disclose the use of AI merely for language polishing, background research on a topic, or reference checking, provided the AI use stays within the ICMJE recommendations. Reviewers are ultimately responsible for the content of their reviews. Recognizing Peer Reviewers Emerging Infectious Diseases has partnered with Publons to make it easier for peer reviewers to track their contributions. EID includes the information Publons needs in the thank-you letters we send to all reviewers. 2025 Reviewers 2024 Reviewers 2023 Reviewers 2022 Reviewers 2021 Reviewers Emerging Infectious Diseases thanks the following reviewers for their support through thoughtful, thorough, and timely reviews in 2025.
